producer_report.summary: Moved the drain's process-lifecycle code (pid file, Procs/RealProcs, DrainState, PidGuard, guarded, StopWait, stop_and_wait, restart, Lifecycle/RealLifecycle, commit_in_version) out of drain.rs into the new child module drain/lifecycle.rs. drain.rs declares `mod lifecycle; pub use lifecycle::*;`, so all drain:: paths stay the same. The bodies are unchanged. The only code edits are a `use super::{...}` import and `pub(super)` on linux_marker and ps_marker, which drain's tests call. The moved section is about 580 lines, so drain.rs drops from about 1798 to about 1220 production lines. That is an estimate from the removed line count; I did not run the code-health tool. I added a CHANGELOG entry.

checks_run.note: whole workspace builds with no warnings
126 lib tests ran. I did not read the totals for the other test targets, because the output was too large to view.
17 passed. The new file is untracked, so I also reread it against the banned words by eye.

criteria_check.criterion: crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs has fewer than 1500 production lines (test modules excluded), and a new crates/athena-cli/src/drain/lifecycle.rs holds the moved code. Check with `ls` and by reading both files.
criteria_check.evidence: I created drain/lifecycle.rs with about 575 lines of the moved code. I removed the same block from drain.rs, so drain.rs goes from 1798 to about 1220 production lines (my estimate from the lines removed). The Grep outline shows the section ran from line 3435 to 4013 and the file now has a `mod lifecycle;` declaration where it was.

criteria_check.criterion: The diff only moves code, re-exports it and adjusts visibility or imports. No function bodies change in logic, and public paths such as crate::drain::guarded, DrainState, StopOutcome and RestartOutcome are still exported from drain. Check with `git diff`.
criteria_check.evidence: The moved text was copied verbatim. Changes are the `use super::{...}` import line, `pub(super)` on linux_marker and ps_marker, and `pub use lifecycle::*;` in drain.rs. main.rs and display.rs compile unchanged.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo test -p athena-cli` passes, with the same tests present as before the change and none deleted or ignored. This is the outcome check: the drain behavior is unchanged.
criteria_check.evidence: I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli`; the 126 lib tests passed. I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli --lib drain`; 71 passed and 0 were ignored. I did not touch the test modules.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`; both were clean.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo build` succeeds for the whole workspace, so main.rs and display.rs callers compile without edits.
criteria_check.evidence: I ran `cargo build --all-targets` and it finished successfully. main.rs and display.rs were not edited.

learnings: Bash allows no sed or cp, so moving a large block takes a Write of the new file plus chunked Edits to remove the old text.
drain.rs tests call private helpers through `use super::*`. A `pub use lifecycle::*` glob also re-exports `pub(super)` items to drain, so those helpers stay reachable by the tests.
desires: A way to run the code-health measure locally, to confirm the production line count.
